title: Macramé feather earrings
subtitle: Knotted cord feather shapes on metal earring hooks, about 8 cm drop
excerpt: Macramé feather earrings are made by knotting a small number of cords onto an earring ring and then combing the knotted fringe into a feather shape. Each earring takes about 20 minutes once the technique is familiar. The finished drop is about 8 cm.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from standard modern macramé craft practice. Macramé feather earrings are a widely-taught beginner project using lark's head knots and fringe combing.

glossaryTerms.definition: A mounting knot used to attach cord to a ring or rod. Fold the cord in half and pull the fold through the ring, then pass the two ends through the fold and pull tight.
A flat knot made with two working cords around two or more filler cords. The foundation knot of macramé.

and then combing the individual cord strands into a unified feather shape with a fringe comb. The shaping is done with scissors rather than knots: cut the outline of the feather into the cord fringe, then comb the fibres out until they are soft and feathery. A couple of
near the ring create the rachis (the central spine of the feather). Use a 3-ply macramé cotton in white, cream, or a dyed colour.

items.name: Small metal jump rings or earring loops, 8 mm diameter
Fine-tooth fringe comb (a pet slicker brush works well)

content.text: Step 1: Attach cords to the ring

Cut 8 to 10 lengths of cord, each 18 to 20 cm. Fold each cord in half and attach it to the ring with a lark's head knot. Mount them close together along the bottom of the jump ring so that the cords hang in a dense fringe.

Identify the two central cords. Tie two or three square knots around these central cords using the adjacent cords as working cords. This creates a firm central spine about 1 to 2 cm below the ring. The remaining cords form the feather's barbs.

Secure the earring to the macramé board with a T-pin through the ring. Comb downward through the cord fringe with the fringe comb, working from the ring toward the tips, until all three-ply cords are fully separated into individual fibres. Work slowly; pulling too hard on the cords can detach the lark's head knots. Comb from the sides inward toward the central spine to build the feather shape.

Once combed, the fringe will appear as a broad, fluffy mass. Hold the earring against a piece of paper and draw the feather outline: widest in the upper third, narrowing to a point at the tip. Cut the outline with sharp scissors, cutting through all the individual fibres cleanly. Re-comb after cutting to blend any cut ends. The feather should now have a recognisable vane shape with a visible central spine.
Open the jump ring at the top of the earring with jewellery pliers and attach it to the earring hook loop. Close the jump ring. Make the second earring as a mirror of the first.

items.problem: The combed fringe lost its lark's head knots and the cords slipped off the ring
items.cause: The cords were pulled too hard during combing, particularly near the ring
items.fix: Comb from the tips upward toward the knots rather than from the ring downward. Work gently near the knot area and hold the knots with one finger while combing the cords below.

items.problem: The feather shape looks ragged and uneven after cutting
items.cause: The fibres were not fully combed before cutting, leaving some cord strands not fully separated
items.fix: Comb thoroughly before cutting; every individual fibre should be separated and fluffy before the scissors touch the outline. Re-comb after cutting to blend the cut ends.
